text: The user is interested in the latest developments in AI and machine learning, has been taking online courses to improve the user's skills, and wants to stay updated on research and breakthroughs as of 20 August 2023.
The user graduated with a Bachelor's in Computer Science from UCLA in 2020, a degree that took the user four years to complete.
The assistant recommended top AI and machine learning conferences for staying current, including NeurIPS, ICML, ICCV, AAAI and IJCAI.

The assistant also suggested AI and machine learning resources such as arXiv, Papers with Code, JMLR, KDnuggets, Machine Learning Mastery, the AI Alignment Forum, and Andrew Ng's DeepLearning.ai courses on Coursera.
The user is particularly interested in applications of AI in robotics, having been part of a high school robotics team and having enjoyed it.

The assistant recommended robotics research venues and resources, including the IEEE Robotics and Automation Magazine, the International Journal of Robotics Research, the ICRA, IROS and RSS conferences, The Robot Report, Boston Dynamics, NASA Robotics and the Carnegie Mellon Robotics Institute.
The user is also interested in AI applications in healthcare, and has a younger sister who is currently studying biology at Stanford as of 20 August 2023.

The assistant recommended healthcare AI resources such as Nature Medicine, npj Digital Medicine, the Journal of Medical Systems, the AMIA Annual Symposium and the MLHC conference, and listed Google Health, Microsoft Healthcare, Stanford Health Care and the NIH as organisations working in the field.
The user graduated from UCLA in 2020 with a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, earning a GPA of 3.6 out of 4.0 and making the Dean's list for three consecutive semesters.
The user is interested in exploring AI applications in medical imaging and diagnostics, and asked for resources to learn more about that topic as of 20 August 2023.

The assistant recommended online courses on AI in medical imaging, including the University of Edinburgh's AI in Medical Imaging specialisation on Coursera, the University of Michigan's Deep Learning for Medical Imaging course on edX, and MIT OpenCourseWare and Stanford CS231n material.
The assistant suggested medical imaging journals and conferences, including Radiology: Artificial Intelligence, Medical Image Analysis, the MICCAI conference and SPIE Medical Imaging.

The user wants to apply machine learning and deep learning skills, built through Coursera and edX courses, to real-world problems in radiology and oncology within medical imaging and diagnostics, as of 20 August 2023.

The assistant recommended RSNA and AACR as conferences, Radiology: Artificial Intelligence and the Journal of Medical Imaging as journals, and the National Cancer Institute as a research institution for AI in radiology and oncology.

The assistant suggested an edX course titled 'AI in Oncology' from the University of Pennsylvania and an 'AI in Radiology' course from the University of Michigan for learning AI in radiology and oncology.
The user is shopping for gift ideas for coworkers' birthdays, which are coming up soon as of 21 May 2023, and wants something nice that is not too expensive.
During the 2022 holiday season, the user bought five coffee mugs with funny profession-related quotes, one for each coworker, as a holiday gesture.

The assistant suggested ten budget-friendly birthday gift ideas for coworkers, including a personalised desk accessory, gourmet treats, an experience such as tickets to a local sporting event, a desk plant, a subscription and a handwritten note.
The user liked the idea of a customised desk accessory as a coworker birthday gift and asked where to buy one.

The assistant recommended websites for customised desk accessories, including Etsy, Zazzle, Vistaprint, Personalization Mall, Things Remembered, CafePress, Amazon, Mark and Graham and Levenger, as well as local trophy and engraving shops.
The user planned to buy one customised desk accessory for each coworker and asked whether these websites offer discounts or promotions for bulk orders.

The assistant said Zazzle, Personalization Mall, CafePress and Mark and Graham each offer a bulk discount of up to 20% for orders of 10 or more items, and Vistaprint offers up to 50% off bulk orders of 10 or more items.
The assistant said Etsy bulk discounts vary by seller, Things Remembered and Levenger only occasionally offer bulk discounts, and Amazon typically does not offer bulk discounts.
The user wanted to know how long it takes to produce and ship customised desk accessories, so the gifts arrive on time for coworkers' birthdays.
The assistant said customised items usually take 1 to 5 business days to produce, with Zazzle, Vistaprint and CafePress at 1 to 3 business days, and standard shipping takes 3 to 7 business days.
The assistant advised ordering at least 7 to 10 business days before the birthdays, choosing expedited or express shipping where possible, and ordering a proof or sample before placing a bulk order.
The user was still deciding on the design and material for the desk accessories and asked for suggestions suitable for a coworker birthday gift.

The assistant suggested design styles for the desk accessories, including simple and elegant, humorous, inspirational and personalised, and materials including glass or crystal, wood, metal and ceramic.

The user leaned toward a simple and elegant glass or crystal paperweight with a brief message such as 'Happy Birthday' or 'Wishing you a great year ahead' for coworkers' birthdays, and asked for the assistant's opinion.

The assistant agreed the glass or crystal paperweight idea was a good choice and suggested adding a small card with a more personal message, such as 'Thanks for being an amazing colleague and friend!'
The user is trying to get a better grip on finances, especially gift-giving spending, and had noticed spending a lot on gifts lately, as of 26 May 2023.
The user once spent $60 on coffee mugs for coworkers, which was a splurge at the time, but the coworkers loved the mugs.

The assistant proposed a gift budgeting plan that includes setting a budget of around 1 to 2 percent of annual income, allocating funds per occasion, and setting price ranges such as $10 to $20 for coworker gifts, $20 to $50 for friends or family, and $50 to $100 for significant occasions.
The assistant suggested that the user set a lower price range for coworker gifts or explore more affordable options after the $60 coffee mug splurge.
The user liked the idea of allocating gift funds per occasion and asked for help estimating annual gift-giving expenses from past spending habits.

The assistant explained how to estimate annual gift spending: gather 12 months of gift-related expenses, categorise them by occasion, annualise any shorter period, and add a 10 to 20 percent buffer for irregular expenses.

In the past 3 months, the user spent $50 on a best friend's birthday gift, $60 on a brother's anniversary gift, $60 on coworker coffee mugs, $32 on a mother's birthday gift and $75 on a cousin's baby shower gift, totalling $277.
The user also contributed $20 to a group gift for a cousin's baby shower, bringing gift-giving spending for the past 3 months (up to 26 May 2023) to $297.
The assistant annualised the user's $297 three-month gift total to $1,188 per year by multiplying by four, describing it as a rough starting estimate.
The user tends to spend more during holidays such as Christmas, buying gifts for family and close friends, and estimates spending around $200 to $300 on Christmas gifts alone.

The assistant updated the estimated annual gift spending to $1,438 by adding $250, the midpoint of the user's Christmas range, and proposed a 50/30/20 split: $718 for regular gifts, $431 for occasional gifts and $289 for miscellaneous gifts.
The user asked for the $718 regular-gift allocation to be broken down into smaller amounts for specific occasions such as birthdays and holidays.

The assistant split the $718 into $200 for birthdays (about six birthdays at $30 to $40 each), $325 for holidays including Christmas, and $135 for other regular gifts, totalling $660 with a $58 buffer.
The user said the $200 birthday allocation did not cover coworker gifts, which the user also buys, and asked how to adjust the allocation.
The assistant revised the birthday allocation to $350 by adding $150 for coworker gifts, assuming 7 to 10 coworkers at $10 to $20 each, which brought the regular gift total to $810.
While planning the week's schedule on 26 May 2023, the user asked which day the language exchange class with Juan falls on.
The assistant said it could not track the user's personal schedule and suggested checking a calendar, planner, phone reminders or asking Juan directly.
The user recalled that Juan had mentioned meeting during the week of 22 May 2023 to practise conversational dialogues, and asked for tips on improving conversational flow in Spanish.

The assistant gave eight tips for improving Spanish conversational flow, including active listening, practising around a specific topic, and using transitional phrases such as '¿Cómo se dice...?', 'Por cierto' and 'Hablemos de...'.

The assistant suggested the user prepare for the session with Juan by reviewing common topics such as hobbies, travel and daily routines, practising related vocabulary, and preparing a few questions to start the conversation.
The user was unsure whether the language exchange with Juan fell on a Tuesday or a Thursday and asked the assistant to help work out the day.
The user said the language exchange with Juan always takes place in the evening, that the user usually has dinner plans with friends on Thursdays, and that the meeting is probably not on a Thursday.
The user attends a language exchange class at a local language school, where a Colombian tutor named Juan is the partner, and the class meets every Wednesday evening.

In the language exchange, Juan helps the user with Spanish pronunciation and grammar while the user helps Juan with English vocabulary, and the user confirmed the class is on Wednesday evenings as of 26 May 2023.
The user is planning a trip to Colombia and asked for travel tips and Spanish phrases, having a language exchange session with a tutor named Maria during the week of 22 May 2023.

The assistant listed must-visit Colombian destinations as Medellín, Cartagena, the Coffee Region, Tayrona National Park and the Lost City (Ciudad Perdida), and advised avoiding travel alone at night and using reputable taxis or ride-hailing services.
The assistant gave basic Spanish travel phrases, including 'Hola', 'Buenos días', '¿Cuánto cuesta?' (How much does it cost?), 'Agua, por favor' and '¡Gracias!'.
The user said the meeting with Maria is actually on Thursday and asked for common shopping phrases for use in Colombia.

The assistant gave shopping phrases for Colombia, including 'Estoy buscando...' (I'm looking for...), '¿Aceptan tarjetas de crédito?' (Do you accept credit cards?), '¿Es posible un descuento?' (Is a discount possible?) and 'La voy a llevar' (I'll take it).

The assistant advised being ready to haggle in markets, said many Colombian places accept US dollars, and recommended carrying Colombian pesos (COP) because cards may not be accepted in smaller towns.
The user planned to visit the Gold Museum (Museo del Oro) in Bogotá and asked the assistant to explain what it is about.

The assistant said the Gold Museum is part of the Bank of the Republic of Colombia, holds over 55,000 pieces of pre-Columbian goldwork and other artefacts, and is located at Carrera 6 No. 15-88 in La Candelaria.

The assistant gave the Gold Museum's opening hours as 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM Tuesday to Saturday and 10:00 AM to 5:00 PM on Sundays, closed on Mondays, and said free guided tours are offered in Spanish, English and French.

The assistant named the Muisca, Quimbaya and Tairona cultures as key pre-Columbian collections and highlighted the Muisca Raft, described as a golden raft with 1,200 grams of 24-karat gold, as a museum highlight.
The user had heard the Gold Museum is a good place to learn about the history of the Spanish conquest and asked whether it has exhibits on that topic, and for nearby cafés for a quick lunch or snack.

The assistant said the Gold Museum has exhibits on the Spanish arrival and colonisation, the exploitation of gold and resources, and cultural exchange and syncretism between Spanish and indigenous populations.

The assistant recommended cafés and restaurants near the Gold Museum, including Café San Alberto, La Macarena Café, El Cielo and La Puerta Falsa, which it described as a historic café and bakery operating since 1816.
The user planned to visit Plaza de Bolívar after the Gold Museum and asked about its significance and what to expect there.

The assistant described Plaza de Bolívar as Bogotá's main square, named after Simón Bolívar, and surrounded by the Catedral Primada, the Capitolio Nacional and the Palacio Liévano, which it said was once the residence of the Spanish viceroys.
The user planned to grab a snack at a café around Plaza de Bolívar before exploring the surrounding streets and asked about other nearby attractions not to miss.

The assistant recommended attractions in La Candelaria, including Calle del Embudo, Plaza de Chorro de Quevedo, Iglesia de San Francisco, the Museo de la Independencia, Casa de la Moneda and Teatro Colón.
On 22 May 2023 the user finished the last of the chicken fajitas with sautéed onions and bell peppers, which had been made the week of 15 May 2023, and called it the third meal from those fajitas.
The user is trying to reduce food waste and is looking for creative recipe ideas for using up leftover vegetables as of 22 May 2023.

The assistant suggested ten ways to use leftover vegetables, including a veggie frittata, a soup or stew, a roasted veggie wrap, veggie burgers, a quiche or tart, a stir-fry, a grilled veggie salad, veggie cakes, freezing vegetables and veggie broth.
The user liked the veggie frittata idea and wanted to try making one with roasted vegetables, asking which vegetables work best in a frittata.

The assistant said good frittata vegetables include roasted bell peppers, caramelised onions, mushrooms, zucchini, spinach and kale, roasted sweet potatoes, asparagus, broccoli, cauliflower and garlic scapes, using about 1 to 2 cups of chopped vegetables per six-egg frittata.

The assistant gave frittata tips: use room-temperature eggs, avoid overfilling the skillet or overmixing the eggs, use a non-stick or well-seasoned cast-iron pan, and let the frittata cool before slicing.

The user planned to make a frittata with roasted sweet potatoes and caramelised onions, using a sweet potato that had been in the pantry for a while, and said caramelising onions always seems to take forever.

The assistant gave a quick caramelised onion method: heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium-high heat, cook one thinly sliced large onion with a pinch of salt for 5 minutes without stirring, stir for 5 to 7 minutes, then deglaze with about 1 tablespoon of vinegar or wine.
The assistant said sweet onions such as Vidalia or Maui caramelise faster, and that the whole process typically takes about 15 to 20 minutes.
The user has been experimenting with different marinades for grilled chicken breasts and wanted a new recipe to try.

The assistant recommended four chicken breast marinades: lemon-herb, Korean-style gochujang, Indian-inspired yogurt and balsamic glaze, and advised marinating for at least 30 minutes to 2 hours, or overnight for more intense flavour.

The assistant's Korean-style gochujang marinade uses 1/2 cup soy sauce, 1/4 cup gochujang, 2 cloves of minced garlic, 1 tablespoon brown sugar, 1 teaspoon grated ginger and 1/4 teaspoon red pepper flakes (optional).
The user chose to try the Korean-style gochujang marinade, wanting to experiment with gochujang, and already enjoys its sweet and spicy flavour from Korean dishes.

The assistant advised starting with a small amount of gochujang, a thick fermented chilli paste that is hard to tone down once added, and suggested serving the chicken with rice, kimchi or roasted vegetables.
As of 25 May 2023 the user has been meal prepping a lot and has found it to be a huge time saver, and is looking for new lunch recipes to try.

The assistant suggested meal-prep lunch ideas including Korean-style BBQ beef bowls, Indian-style lentil curry, Mexican chicken fajitas, quinoa salad jars, turkey and avocado wraps, Thai coconut soup and pesto chicken pasta.

The assistant also suggested chicken and veggie fried rice and Cajun shrimp and rice bowls as meal-prep lunches, and asked whether the user has any dietary restrictions such as vegetarian, gluten-free or dairy-free.
The user recently made a big batch of lentil soup that lasted five lunches and wants other hearty soup recipes that suit meal prep, as of 25 May 2023.

The assistant recommended seven hearty soups for meal prep: minestrone, black bean and sweet potato, butternut squash and chickpea curry, spicy roasted vegetable, creamy broccoli and potato, white bean and kale, and chicken and rice.
The assistant said the meal-prep soups can be refrigerated or frozen for up to 5 days and suggested serving them with crusty bread or a green salad.
The user was intrigued by the butternut squash and chickpea curry soup, having never had butternut squash in a soup before, and asked for tips on roasting the squash.

The assistant advised roasting butternut squash at 400°F (200°C) for 45 to 50 minutes, or at 425°F (220°C) for 30 to 35 minutes when short on time, after halving it lengthwise, oiling it and seasoning with salt and pepper.
The user asked whether a pre-mixed curry powder could be used in the butternut squash and chickpea curry soup, or whether individual spices such as cumin, coriander and turmeric would be better.

The assistant recommended individual spices for the butternut squash and chickpea curry soup: 1 teaspoon ground cumin, 1/2 teaspoon ground coriander, 1/2 teaspoon ground turmeric and optional 1/4 teaspoon cayenne, toasted in oil or ghee before adding onions and garlic.
The user has been making cauliflower rice a lot to reduce carbohydrate intake and wanted new methods for preparing it.

The assistant described four cauliflower rice methods: microwaving on high for 3 to 4 minutes, sautéing over medium-high heat until golden, roasting at 400°F (200°C) for 20 to 25 minutes, and steaming for 5 to 7 minutes.
The user enjoys experimenting with seasonings and spices on cauliflower rice and asked for protein sources and vegetables to add to it.

The assistant suggested protein sources for cauliflower rice, including grilled chicken, pan-seared shrimp, roasted tofu and cooked sausages, plus vegetables such as roasted broccoli, Brussels sprouts or asparagus, sautéed mushrooms and steamed green beans.
